items.title: Dax Shepard Admits He’s in a ‘Depression’ Amid Kristen Bell Marriage Backlash
items.summary:
Dax Shepard is opening up about the backlash over his marriage to Kristen Bell and how it has affected his mental health.

“One of the elements is a media storm about this continuing narrative that I’m an abusive husband, which is, like, very offensive,” Shepard, 51, said during the Monday, November 23, episode of his “Armchair Expert” podcast after cohost Monica Padman said he’s “in a depression” right now.

The Parenthood alum went on to recall the backlash he received last year after Bell, 46, shared an anniversary tribute in which she quoted her husband as saying, “I would never kill you. A lot of men have killed their wives at a certain point. Even though I’m heavily incentivized to kill you, I never would.”

The post drew criticism as fans accused Shepard of abuse and making light of domestic violence.

A Look Back at the Times Kristen Bell and Dax Shepard Defended Their Marriage 

“Kristen had a joke years ago on an anniversary. We were watching Dateline one time, and you know, everyone kills their rich spouse,” Shepard said on Monday. “This was actually me complimenting Kristen … So we’re watching it, and I go, you know, ‘I’m heavily incentivized to kill you, but I’m not going to.’ And she said that was one of the most romantic things anyone said to her. So she posts that.”

Looking back at the aftermath of the controversial post, Shepard added, “Someone all of a sudden’s like, ‘Oh, it’s domestic abuse awareness month.’ Then she’s on the Today show and now we’re in this big thing.” (Bell skipped a Today show appearance amid the backlash.)

Jon Kopaloff/Getty Images…
items.t: Dax Shepard Admits He’s in a ‘Depression’ Amid Kristen Bell Marriage Backlash

items.title: Missing Coach Travis Turner's Wife Addresses His Disappearance 1-Year Later
items.summary:
One year after Travis Turner allegedly vanished into the woods behind his Virginia home, his wife, Leslie Caudill Turner , is telling her side of the story.  

“I just don’t have any closure, I cry every day,” Leslie told the Daily Mail in a story published on Thursday, November 19.  

Travis, 46, disappeared on November 20, 2025, allegedly last seen by his family fleeing while carrying a rifle . Shortly after he went missing, Travis – the former head football coach at Union High School in Big Stone Gap, Virginia – was charged with five counts of child pornography and five counts of using a computer to solicit a minor.  

“It’s like day one all over again,” Leslie said of the one-year anniversary of her husband’s disappearance. “Every day that I’ve not been told that there’s a body found, I still have a little bit of hope. But I don’t think he’d be able to go an entire year without letting somebody know he’s okay.” 

Expert Predicts Grim Fate for Missing Travis Turner as 1-Year Mark Approaches 

She continued, “We’re already grieving like he’s dead.” 

Leslie and Travis share three children: sons Bailey , 24, and Grayden , 21, and daughter Brynlee , 12. Since her husband disappeared, Leslie has kept “his stuff where he left it.”

items.title: Montel Williams Opens Up About Daughter's Addiction Battle, Blames Himself
items.summary:
Montel Williams is sharing a rare glimpse into his daughter’s addiction that he believes stemmed from medications she was prescribed as a child to treat her epilepsy.

“As a parent, you know, I of course didn’t understand and didn’t do the right things, I think,” Williams, 70, shared in Us ’ exclusive sneak peek of the Tuesday, November 24, episode of the “ We’re Out of Time ” podcast. “Not even realizing that I’m the one, in some ways, by allowing the doctors to prescribe medication that she was prescribed when she was young, I’m the one that turned her into a drug addict.”

Podcast host Richard Taite , who serves as the chairman of Carrara Treatment and 1 Method Centers , quickly stopped his guest from putting the blame on himself.

“You did the best you could at the time. You’re in love with your daughter,” Taite explained in the sneak peek. “You’re in love with your family. You’re one of the most decent people I’ve ever met. I think you’re going to leave that with me.”

Now, the former talk show host is grateful to see his daughter in a much healthier space and “100 percent sober.”

items.title: America's Most Reviewed GLP-1 Company Just Announced Free Prescription NAD+
items.summary:

GLP-1 medications changed what is possible in weight loss. Semaglutide and Tirzepatide took a struggle that was framed for decades as a matter of willpower and turned it into a matter of biology, and the results have been unlike anything the field has seen. For millions of Americans, the question is no longer whether these medications work. It is which company to trust with them, and what to do about the one part of the journey almost nobody warns you about.

The part of the journey nobody posts about 

The entire point of a GLP-1 is that you eat dramatically less. The food noise quiets, the portions shrink, and the scale finally starts moving. What the before-and-after posts leave out is simple arithmetic: less food in can mean less fuel in. Many patients describe the same pattern in almost the same words. Flat by mid-afternoon. Napping when they never used to nap. Eating like a bird and feeling like a rock.

That is not the medication failing. That is the medication working, colliding with the fact that your cells still have to produce energy from whatever you give them. Which is exactly where a molecule the longevity world has been obsessed with for years enters the story.

What NAD+ actually is 

NAD+ is a molecule found in every cell in your body. It is one of the central coenzymes your cells rely on in the process of converting the food you eat into usable energy, and your natural levels decline as you get older. That combination, central to cellular energy, falling with age, is why NAD+ became a fixture of the longevity and wellness world long before most…
items.t: America's Most Reviewed GLP-1 Company Just Announced Free Prescription NAD+

items.summary:
Selling the OC ’s Kayla Cardona is asking for support after her 20-year-old son, Jordan, faced a life-threatening medical emergency.

“What began as unexpected internal bleeding quickly turned into a terrifying fight for survival,” Kayla, 37, wrote via a GoFundMe page. “As suspected, Meckel’s diverticulum did NOT appear on Jordan’s CT scans, colonoscopy or endoscopy. It was only during emergency intestinal surgery that doctors confirmed Meckel’s diverticulum, the very condition they had been urged to investigate.”

According to the Cleveland Clinic , Meckel’s diverticulum is a congenital defect in the small intestine. It occurs in 2 percent of the population and only 2 percent of people who have it develop complications or symptoms.

“Throughout his hospitalization, Jordan required nine blood transfusions, three units of plasma, and one platelet transfusion to survive,” Kayla wrote. “Although Jordan is finally home, his journey toward healing and recovery is just beginning.”

Truly an angel on earth.”
